mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met, or the trigger is met but returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its moving average for six months, or positive returns occur in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% for two months, or positive returns occur in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both above 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS are above their moving averages for three months, or positive returns occur in fewer than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for four consecutive months signals a deteriorating labor market and weakening consumer confidence, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for four months, or positive returns occur in more than 40% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals a prolonged housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its moving average for eight months, or positive returns occur in more than 35% of such episodes.
